name: the-events-calendar
notes: Production-readiness audit 2026-08-22: the official WordPress.org The Events Calendar 6.17.2 artifact is pinned at SHA-256 f67f2668fc777505a6e0f2cc8c7c39db869a1b186b2444f9d5e138d32bcaabaa. The one-patch range admits only the inspected artifact; widening requires a new schema, regenerator, lifecycle, and request-behavior exercise.

Grind R3-B (task #91). Real schema verified live on The Events Calendar 6.17.2 (free, wp.org slug `the-events-calendar`) — every table/option/meta-key claim below was empirically checked (SHOW TABLES, DESCRIBE, create real content and SELECT before/after, read plugin source), not carried over from the task brief's own shorthand, which turned out to be wrong on one point: there are NO `tribe_*` custom tables at all (SHOW TABLES LIKE 'wp_tribe\_%' returns zero rows) — venues (`tribe_venue`) and organizers (`tribe_organizer`) are plain CPTs, exactly as expected, referenced from an event's postmeta via `_EventVenueID`/`_EventOrganizerID` (both `ref: post`, generic post refs — the ref system is keyed by entity kind, not specific post_type, same as `_thumbnail_id`). Recurring events are an Events Calendar PRO (paid) feature: free TEC's own `Single_Event_Migration_Strategy::__construct()` (see the tec_events/tec_occurrences note below) explicitly throws 'Attempting to run Single Event strategy for recurring event. Install and activate the latest version of Events Calendar PRO' the moment `_EventRecurrence` postmeta carries any `rules` — confirmed by reading the source, not by installing Pro to test it; free TEC simply never writes that meta key, so the boundary is enforced by the plugin's own absence of the feature, not by anything Duo does.

tec_events / tec_occurrences (the central finding of this round — DERIVED, but with a HARD query-availability dependency, not a soft cache): TEC 6.x's 'Custom Tables v1' architecture maintains two custom tables alongside the classic `_Event*` postmeta, populated automatically the moment a `tribe_events` post is created via the repository (`tribe_events()->set_args([...])->create()`) — verified live: creating one event instantly produced matching rows in both `tec_events` (event_id PK, post_id UNIQUE, start/end dates, timezone, duration, hash) and `tec_occurrences` (occurrence_id PK, event_id + post_id FK-shaped columns, its own start/end dates, a UNIQUE hash) with byte-identical date values to the classic postmeta. The FIRST empirical test (per task #91's own suggestion) was deleting both rows for a throwaway event and checking whether TEC's own machinery rebuilds them — it does NOT self-heal on any WordPress-native trigger: neither an ordinary `wp post update` resave (fires `save_post`, TEC does not hook table regeneration to it) NOR TEC's own repository query (`tribe_events()->where('id', $id)->first()`) could find the post afterward. The second, sharper test: `wp post list --post_type=tribe_events` — a PLAIN WP_Query, nothing TEC-view-specific — returned ZERO rows for a post independently confirmed (via `wp post get`) to still exist with `post_type=tribe_events`. TEC's `WP_Query\Provider` filters query SQL for this post type to require a matching `tec_occurrences` row; without one, the post is not merely poorly-rendered on a calendar view, it is INVISIBLE to WP_Query itself, admin post list included. This is a materially harder dependency than any derived custom table this project has classified before (nf3_upgrades' stale-cache and wc_product_meta_lookup's query-optimization role are both soft — the owning post/row remains fully findable either way). A REAL regeneration path exists and was verified working: TEC ships `TEC\Events\Custom_Tables\V1\Migration\Strategies\Single_Event_Migration_Strategy`, built for exactly this recovery scenario (upgrading a pre-6.0 site, whose events predate these tables, is a first-class supported case) — its two operative calls, `Event::upsert(['post_id'], Event::data_from_post($post_id))` then `Event::find($post_id, 'post_id')->occurrences()->save_occurrences()`, read straight from the post's own postmeta (bypassing the broken occurrence-dependent query path entirely) and were confirmed live to fully restore both tables and re-establish `wp post list` visibility for the same post.

Why this manifest classifies tec_events/tec_occurrences/tec_kv_cache as 'runtime'/'derived' (silently excluded from capture — Snapshot.php gives no special meaning to any class value besides authored_snapshot/authored_snapshot_meta, so this is the same 'safe, honest, silent-exclude' choice manifests/woocommerce.json already made for wc_product_meta_lookup) rather than declaring authored_snapshot: these tables have NO independent authored content of their own — every column is copied straight from the post/postmeta that already round-trips through Duo's ordinary post machinery — so authored_snapshot's per-row identity/ledger machinery would be pure duplication, not new coverage. The genuine gap is NOT capture (there is nothing here worth capturing) — it is that DESIGN.md's own vocabulary ('derived — rebuilt') implies a target environment ends up correct after a rebuild pass, and today's manifest grammar has no way to express 'this derived table has a hard per-entity query-availability dependency; the rebuild pass MUST run a synthesis step for every entity of this post type before the applied entities are actually usable, and must fail LOUDLY if the synthesis mechanism disappears in a future plugin version' — as opposed to the existing `rebuilders` mechanism's actual shape: a single blanket wp-cli command with no per-entity substitution and no version-compatibility guard. Reaching TEC's regeneration path from a manifest today would mean smuggling a non-public, internal namespaced class (`TEC\Events\Custom_Tables\V1\Migration\Strategies\Single_Event_Migration_Strategy` — no `@api` stability contract, could rename/vanish in a future TEC release with no warning) through a `wp eval` string inside `rebuilders` — syntactically legal, but exactly the fragile, unguarded, plugin-internals-reaching-through-a-generic-string-field pattern manifests/woocommerce.json's own `_price` note already flagged as the wrong instinct for a DIFFERENT reason (there, the payoff was unnecessary; here the payoff is real and necessary, but the fragility concern is the same and arguably worse, since correctness — not merely staleness — is at stake). Characterized as an engine gap rather than forced into the manifest: escalated to team-lead from grind round R3-B, with the acceptance criteria exactly as stated above.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE, stated plainly and demonstrated live in the grind script: applying a captured `tribe_events` post to a fresh target environment (posts + postmeta round-trip perfectly, exactly as designed) leaves that event genuinely invisible on the target — not merely un-optimized — until the SAME manual regeneration step verified above is run by hand. The grind driver demonstrates the break, then the fix, exactly like grind round R1-B's pa_* attribute pre-provisioning gap: 'the honest mitigation... a manual step, not an automated one.'

DUO-3234 plus the 2026-08-22 production-readiness stale-row regression: `post_types.tribe_events.regen_dependency` declares an always-on-write refresh, because row existence is insufficient — an adopted target event can already have a tec_occurrences row whose dates disagree with the applied post meta. `regenerator: "the-events-calendar"` resolves to `manifests/regenerators/the-events-calendar.php`, which wraps the exact two verified-live calls this note already named (`Event::upsert()` + `Event::find()->occurrences()->save_occurrences()`), re-confirmed against the real TEC 6.17.2 source (src/Events/Custom_Tables/V1/Migration/Strategies/Single_Event_Migration_Strategy.php:70-100) before being wrapped. The regenerator additionally compares the single free-TEC occurrence row's start/end values with `_EventStartDate`/`_EventEndDate`; a present-but-stale row fails loudly. `verify: {table: "tec_occurrences", column: "post_id"}` remains the generic existence backstop. tec_events/tec_occurrences themselves stay derived and excluded from capture — this declaration changes only the target postcondition.

tec_kv_cache: a generic key/value cache table (cache_key PK, value, expiration) — confirmed by DESCRIBE and by its own name; holds zero site-builder content by construction. Classified runtime (a cache, not a per-entity query-availability dependency like tec_events/tec_occurrences — losing it just means TEC recomputes whatever it cached).

tribe_events_calendar_options (a single option, TEC's main settings blob): classified env WHOLESALE rather than partially-authored, the same call manifests/polylang.json and manifests/yoast.json already made for their own mixed-content option blobs (v0's options model classifies a whole option name at once; there is no per-sub-key capture/exclude split without json_refs/key_refs declaring EVERY position). The live value on this round's fixture, read raw (not guessed): a mix of genuinely site-builder-authored settings (`tribeEnableViews`, `viewOption`, `dateWithYearFormat`), env/version bookkeeping (`schema-version`, `previous_ecp_versions`), RUNTIME-COMPUTED fields that reflect the site's current event set (`earliest_date`/`latest_date`/`earliest_date_markers`/`latest_date_markers` — these visibly changed as events were added during this round, confirming they are a live cache, not authored config) — and, notably, `google_maps_js_api_key`, a live-formatted Google Maps API key (`AIzaSy...`, the real Google API key prefix) present on a FRESH install with no Maps configuration ever performed. This is DESIGN.md section 1's own worked example verbatim ('API key in options → env-bound secret'), found empirically rather than needing to be manufactured as a test case. Whether this specific key is TEC's own shared/rate-limited default or something else was not independently verified (out of scope to probe a third party's live API key) — the classification holds either way: it is not site-builder-authored content, and capturing it into a git-committed canonical state would leak a credential-shaped value regardless of its provenance. Classifying the whole option env is what keeps it out of captured state without needing to prove liveness.

tec_ct1_events_table_schema_version / tec_ct1_migration_state / tec_ct1_occurrences_table_schema_version / tec_timed_tec_custom_tables_v1_initialized: env — Custom Tables v1's own schema-version and one-time-migration bookkeeping, directly related to the tec_events/tec_occurrences finding above (these are what TEC reads to decide whether the custom-tables migration has already run on THIS environment) but themselves plain env-local markers, not content.

stellar_schema_version_stellarwp-shepherd-tec-tasks / stellar_schema_version_tec-kv-cache: env — StellarWP (TEC's parent company) shared-library schema-version markers for the background-job ('Shepherd') and kv-cache subsystems; same species as woocommerce_db_version.

stellarwp_telemetry / stellarwp_telemetry_last_send / stellarwp_telemetry_the-events-calendar_show_optin: runtime — telemetry opt-in state and send-timestamp bookkeeping, auto-managed, never site-builder-authored config.
tribe_last_generate_rewrite_rules / tribe_last_save_post / tribe_last_updated_option: runtime — internal cache-invalidation timestamps (when various caches were last rebuilt), not content.

_EventShowMap / _EventShowMapLink: declared lint_ok true, reactively, after `wp duo lint` actually flagged both on this round's own 3-event fixture (matches=post:1 'Hello world!') — both are boolean 0/1 display-toggle flags TEC sets on every event by default; reviewed and confirmed genuinely not refs, the same escape hatch as manifests/ninja-forms.json's BIT(1) columns and manifests/woocommerce.json's `queryId`.

_EventOrigin / _OrganizerOrigin / _VenueOrigin: a plain string TEC stamps on every event/venue/organizer it creates ('events-calendar') identifying the creation source (vs. an import from another calendar system) — static per-entity provenance, not env-bound, not a ref: authored.

post_meta absent entirely when unset, not written empty: confirmed live — an event created with no venue/organizer (this round's 'Community Meetup' fixture) carries ZERO `_EventVenueID`/`_EventOrganizerID` postmeta rows, not empty-string rows, matching the ordinary WordPress 'absent key = unset ref' convention the engine's ref-token machinery already assumes.

Version window widened 2026-08-24 from the one-release >=6.17.2 <6.17.3 to >=6.17.2 <6.17.4, on evidence, not on inertia: 6.17.3 (official wp.org artifact, SHA-256 2db436c929797bfc5311be942158c474716e61c2f289f7d05c3a08d29b2ad687) is the only release upstream has published above the previously inspected 6.17.2 artifact. The adapter surface was probed the same way manifests/code-snippets.json probed class-db.php before widening ITS window: src/Events/Custom_Tables/V1/** is byte-identical across the two artifacts, Single_Event_Migration_Strategy.php (the file the tec_events/tec_occurrences note above cites at :70-100, and the exact path manifests/regenerators/the-events-calendar.php wraps) hashes to f307a323aecb78f3004abea04d002e78d1a90d417baa7c6c22f3796db4cf3c12 in both, and Events::SCHEMA_VERSION/Occurrences::SCHEMA_VERSION stay 1.0.1/1.0.3 -- so both env-class schema-version options this manifest declares resolve unchanged. The only non-translation, non-changelog code deltas are src/Tribe/Views/V2/{Url,View,Template/Title,Widgets/Service_Provider}.php, front-end view rendering that touches no option, post_meta, table or schema call this manifest declares. Exercised at both edges by sandbox/tests/certify/certify_version_matrix.sh (VMATRIX_MANIFEST=the-events-calendar), including a populated 6.17.2 -> 6.17.3 in-place upgrade that must refuse as code_drift, redeploy under --force-code-drift, and then produce an empty plan in all seven buckets. Widening past 6.17.4 requires the same probe against the next artifact.

Production-readiness closure 2026-08-23 supersedes the historical one-artifact and whole-option notes above. Official WordPress.org 6.17.2 and 6.17.3 are the exact admitted artifacts; their Custom Tables v1 implementation is byte-identical, both boundaries and a populated 6.17.2 -> 6.17.3 in-place upgrade are exercised, and the exclusive 6.17.4 maximum cannot silently admit a future 6.17.4 release. Official 6.17.1 is the adjacent lower refusal control; 6.17.3 was the latest published artifact at review time.

tribe_events_calendar_options remains environment-owned as a whole, but the reviewed sub_keys below now carry the free plugin's stable human-authored presentation, editor, SEO, category-color, default-linked-post, and timezone settings. Credentials, Event Aggregator remote-import state, event-cleaner schedules, schema/version markers, telemetry, date-range caches, and undeclared add-on keys remain target-owned and are never overwritten by apply.

TEC 6.17.2/6.17.3 free ships Category Colors as a native feature. tribe_events_cat and its five exact tec-events-cat-colors-* term-meta keys are authored state; the interpreter rejects malformed colors, priorities, and flags before compilation. Events Calendar Pro recurrence, Event Tickets state, Event Aggregator records and credentials, legacy Category Colors plugin residue, third-party add-ons, and multisite remain outside this contract and refuse rather than receiving inferred authority.

Event, venue, and organizer deletion remains deliberately unsupported. Duo's generic post deletion is hook-free while TEC and optional add-ons own occurrence cleanup and reverse-reference behavior; the batch regenerator refuses any deletion context before mutation, and conformance proves no tombstone or partial target change is produced.
